answer: Picture a reputation ledger where trusted agents shade jade and flagged ones darken to sable. Sybil resistance comes from bonding: each new identity must lock a refundable stake that unlocks only after sustained honest trade. An attacker spinning up a grove of fakes pays one full bond per head, and any node that turns sable from fraud forfeits its stake, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds while one real agent amortizes a single stake across its lifetime.
